what: apr vs llama.cpp, qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct Q4_K_M, one client both sides
instrument: apr test llm bench (GH-876 Milestone 2) — the SAME OpenAI client, prompts and clock drives both servers
protocol: scripts/llama_pin.toml [protocol.http]: profile medium (128 in/128 out), warmup 15s, 3 x 30s, cooldown 10s, concurrency 1, streaming

mechanism_engaged.note: Neither side is labelled by intent. Each is a line the runtime printed.
mechanism_engaged.llamacpp: load_tensors: offloaded 29/29 layers to GPU; device CUDA0 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090)
mechanism_engaged.apr: Enabling optimized CUDA acceleration (PAR-111) ... CUDA optimized model ready
mechanism_engaged.isolation: measured SEQUENTIALLY; GPU returned to ~650 MiB between lanes, so neither held VRAM while the other ran

headline: apr reaches 0.650x llama.cpp on DECODE and 0.275x on PREFILL. The gap is not uniform: decode is 1.54x behind, prefill 3.64x behind, and apr holds 3.08x the VRAM for the same quantized weights.
corrects: The 11.8 tok/s figure reported on 2026-08-24 was an END-TO-END rate that included ~9.7s of model load. apr's actual decode rate here is 103.3 tok/s — 2.6x the ~40 tok/s 7B reference in CLAUDE.md, not below it. The parity gap is real but it is against llama.cpp's 158.9, not against apr's history.
